text:
lina: Nightly eval (v18b bring-up) flagged a big regression on the "content-guided" promptset. failure rate jumped from ~24% -> 52% for structured JSON outputs.
nightly-bot: auto-report: eval_id=eval-2026-05-12-03, commit=abcdef123456, metric=structured_json_pass_rate, baseline=0.76, current=0.48, alert=#eng-ml
omar: quick look: tokenizer mapping changed in this bring-up. vocab size +5k, several merges removed. I see key tokens used in the promptset got split differently.
hannah: can you paste a before/after sample generation? small diff helps triage.
omar: sure — before (v17):
```
{"answer": "{\"title\": \"Project Plan\", \"steps\": [\"define scope\", \"design\"]}"}
```
after (v18b):
```
{"answer": "{ \"title\" : \"Project Plan\" , \"steps\" : [ \"define scop\", \"design\" ] }"}
```
omar: note the token split\n- "scope" -> "scop" + "e" in the middle of the structured field -> downstream JSON parser fails in eval harness
raj: also saw change in layernorm epsilon in the weight merge commit — commit message says "blend with v17 base, adjust ln eps=1e-6". that could affect generation stability for some prefixes.
lina: good catch. two hypotheses: tokenizer resplit introducing broken tokens in anchor prompts OR weight blend shifting probabilities on boundary tokens.
hannah: plan: (1) run eval with old tokenizer + new weights, (2) run eval with new tokenizer + old weights, (3) run with both new to reproduce. that isolates cause.
infra-bot: queued job eval-compare-1765432199-1: docker run redwood/eval:nightly --eval-id eval-compare-1 --model-ref abcdef123456 --tokenizer-ref v17-tokenizer --promptset content-guided --seed 42
omar: quick local run (new weights + old tokenizer) -> partial regression: pass_rate 70% (was 48%). suggests tokenizer is big factor.
hannah: great. I will run new tokenizer + old weights next.
hannah: results: new tokenizer + v17 weights -> pass_rate 46% (so still bad). so both changes matter but tokenizer change looks primary for these prompts.
raj: maybe the tokenizer merges removed some multiword tokens that preserve JSON boundaries. check merge table diff: `git show abcdef123456:tokenizer/merges.txt` vs `v17:tokenizer/merges.txt`.
omar: diff shows 38 merges removed that overlapped with punctuation+alpha combos. example: "\"steps\":` previously tokenized as ["\"","steps","\":"] now split into ["\"","step","s","\":"].
lina: that explains the "scop->scop e" break too.
hannah: mitigation options: 1) revert tokenizer merges for this release, 2) add promptset-specific tokenizer alias (map common structured tokens to single token), 3) patch evals to tolerate whitespace tokens (not ideal).
raj: from weight side, I'll re-run a tiny randomized eval to verify layernorm epsilon impact. adding a single commit that reverts ln eps change and see.
infra-bot: queued job eval-compare-1765432199-2: docker run redwood/eval:nightly --eval-id eval-compare-2 --model-ref abcdef123456-eps-revert --tokenizer-ref v18-tokenizer --promptset content-guided
omar: temporary hotfix: we can ship with v18 weights + v17 tokenizer to customers on Dedicated until tokenizer change is safe. Need ops note.
lina: agree. Raj/hannah — please open PRs: (A) tokenizer revert candidate (small merge delta), (B) ops configuration to pin tokenizer mapping for dedicated/reserved pools. include evaluation numbers.
hannah: PRs opened: #3421 (tokenizer-revert-candidate) and #3422 (pin-tokenizer-for-dedicated). attached bench results in PR description.
raj: weight-side: will test ln-eps revert and post numbers in PR #3423 if it helps.
lina: thanks — next steps: block v18b auto-roll for hosted until we get a passing eval; allow dedicated pinning shortcut. I'll update eng-release channel.
omar: sample command I used locally:
```
python -m redwood.eval.run \
  --eval-id quick --model-ref abcdef123456 --tokenizer-ref v17-tokenizer \
  --promptset content-guided --output out.json
cat out.json | jq '.metrics.structured_json_pass_rate'
```
lina: adding ticket: ML-7623 "v18b tokenizer merges -> structured JSON failures". linking PRs.
hannah: I'll also add a small unit test in the promptset harness that detects token splits across punctuation for JSON keys.
lina: nice. keep updates here. if anyone needs raw samples I pushed them to gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/ml/18b-json-samples
omar: one more note: some customer prompts that interleave code blocks also showed extra whitespace tokens; might be related.
infra-bot: rolling back auto-ship flag for v18b on hosted: DONE
lina: thanks all. we'll reconvene after the tokenizer PR review. :thumbsup:
